findings.F1: Before fees the book earns money, but fees take more than it gains: the 8,418 trades, all long, make +0.079% each gross (t 2.61) and −0.101% each net, against about 0.18% of fees per round trip. Summed over the bars, the position gained 1.97 against 3.42 of fees.
findings.F2: The fee loss is the same on every coin, so no coin carries the failure on its own: gross per trade runs from +0.041% (BTC) to +0.118% (XRP), and net per trade from −0.139% (BTC) to −0.062% (XRP).
findings.F3: The book holds every trade for exactly 2 hours, entering at the 20:00 bar's close and leaving at the 22:00 bar's close. That means each day pays one full round of fees for a single 2-hour move. The average absolute move over those 2 hours is 0.71%, of which the forecast's edge is only a small part.
findings.F4: The rebound grows steadily with the depth of the fall. Across quintiles of the standardised 3-day fall, the 2-hour return from 21:00 rises from 0.034% to 0.058%, 0.081%, 0.112% and 0.164%. The baseline at that hour is 0.021%, and the top quintile's excess has t 4.31 over 1,702 cases.
findings.F5: Only the deepest falls come near covering the fee, and only when the position is held longer. In the top quintile the return from 21:00 reaches 0.190% after 4 hours (excess t 4.23), 0.212% after 12 hours (t 3.21) and 0.248% after 24 hours (t 1.95, with a 0.098% baseline). The lowest quintile reaches only 0.041% after 4 hours.
findings.F6: Measuring the fall by its raw size gives the same grading. By quintile of the raw 3-day return (mean −0.6% up to −11.4%), the 4-hour return from 21:00 rises from 0.060% to 0.163%, and the 12-hour return from 0.048% to 0.181%.

ideas.idea: For a coin with a 3-day fall, the return over the 4 hours from 21:00 UTC is positive, and the deeper the 3-day fall, the larger that rise, rising most steeply for the deepest falls. The rise is roughly five times larger after the deepest fifth of falls than after the shallowest.
ideas.consequence: The late-evening rebound after a deep fall is worth a trade only when it is held about 4 hours and only after the deepest falls, because a shallow fall's rebound is smaller than the cost of trading it.
ideas.name: deep-fall late-evening four-hour rebound

ideas.idea: For a coin with a 3-day fall, the return over the 12 hours from 21:00 UTC is positive, and the deeper the 3-day fall, the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying a deep 3-day fall in the late US evening could hold through the Asian session and catch a move about four times larger than the 2-hour one, with one round of fees.
ideas.name: overnight rebound after deep falls
